description: The visible mode registry. A mode names the workflow shape a dispatch belongs to; the phase (BUILD/GATE) names the concurrency state. They are orthogonal and both are required on every orchestrator decision and dispatch record. No mode is inferred from prose, and no role may run a mode that is not listed for it.

parked.meaning: The task is deliberately stopped with no active work and no active capability. It is not blocked, not failed, and not done. Only a human-authored proof record or owner instruction resumes it; the orchestrator cannot unpark its own decision.
parked.resume: 10-resume.md with the human-authored resume record ref; the resumed task gets a new capability at the live head/tree, never the parked capability.

campaign.statement: One hacker campaign per release train at the BUILD->GATE boundary. The release-engineer runs once per boundary, not once per task, and spawns exactly one campaign that attacks every task in the train together to find seams between changes. Auditor -> hacker only in BUG_FINDING. Never per task, per flow, or per batch.

INTAKE.exit: one classified route with a mode and SOP id

RESUME.exit: one recovered task and its owning mode

FEATURE.exit: release-train trigger or a named refusal

BUGFIX.exit: delta PASS or a named refusal

SPEC_COMPLETION.exit: clean re-check or a named refusal

DELTA_AUDIT.exit: delta verdict for the new head/tree

DRAIN.exit: drain R5 guard verified or a named unreproducible/refusal

EVALUATION.exit: one evaluation record with routed findings

RELEASE.exit: proof-recorded release result MERGED or REFUSED

PARK.exit: HALT action with reason_code PARKED and task status parked

rules: Every orchestrator-decision and dispatch record names one mode from this file and one phase from phases.json.
A role may run only a mode in its modes[].roles list; a missing mode is a stop, not an implicit grant.
INTAKE selects exactly one other mode; INTAKE itself does no work.
RESUME may select any mode except INTAKE; it never invents a task.
RELEASE is the only mode in GATE; ESCALATION and PARK may halt any phase.
PARK never leaves active work behind: no capability, auditor, K1 run, or builder session remains active.

The hacker is dispatched as one campaign per release train at the BUILD->GATE boundary, never per task, per flow, or per batch: the release-engineer is its parent in RELEASE, the auditor in BUG_FINDING; the orchestrator never dispatches it.
